_comment: Identity & governance matrix per gateway vendor: SSO / SCIM / RBAC / audit logs, and which pricing tier gates each ('the SSO tax'). Control-plane features only — data-plane auth plugins (APISIX openid-connect, Higress key-auth, etc.) protect proxied APIs, not the gateway's own console, and are deliberately excluded. All claims from primary vendor sources (docs, pricing pages, OSS config files), accessed on the as_of date. 'not documented' = the vendor's docs are silent, NOT a confirmed 'no'. Tier gating moves without announcement — verify against live docs before signing.

legend.sso: single sign-on to the gateway's admin/control plane (protocols + IdPs); NOT auth for proxied API traffic
legend.scim: automated user/group provisioning + deprovisioning from an IdP directory
legend.rbac: roles and permission scoping in the control plane (org/team/workspace/key granularity)
legend.audit_logs: logs of administrative actions (who changed what), incl. retention + export path
legend.tier: the vendor's own pricing-tier wording for where the feature unlocks
legend.source: primary URLs backing the cell, accessed on as_of

vendors.type: self-hosted (OSS + Enterprise license key, same Docker image)
vendors.pricing_tiers: Open Source (free, self-hosted) / Enterprise (custom pricing, 30-day trial, license key; self-hosted or air-gapped)

sso.value: Admin UI SSO: Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, generic OIDC, and SAML 2.0
sso.tier: Free for up to 5 users (since v1.76.0: 'SSO is now Free for up to 5 users'), then Enterprise ('Beyond that, an enterprise license is required')

scim.value: /scim endpoints provision/update/deprovision users and teams; documented IdPs: Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, OneLogin, Keycloak, Auth0; SCIM removal also deletes the user's API keys
scim.tier: Enterprise — exact wording: 'SCIM support requires a premium license.'

rbac.value: Global proxy roles (proxy_admin, proxy_admin_viewer, internal_user) + org/team roles (org_admin, team_admin) + key-level scoping (user / team-service-account / user+team keys)
rbac.tier: Global roles and basic teams/virtual keys free OSS; org/team roles Enterprise — exact wording: 'Organization/Team specific roles are premium features.'

audit_logs.value: Create/Update/Delete/Regenerate on Keys, Teams, Users, Models; viewable in UI; export via S3 callback (JSON per event); enterprise docs add retention policies

vendors.notes: Enterprise = same Docker image unlocked by license key. OSS→Enterprise auth line in docs: OSS 'API keys', Enterprise 'SSO + SCIM, OIDC/JWT'. The 5-user free-SSO carve-out removes the SSO tax for tiny teams only.

vendors.type: OSS gateway (data plane only) + hosted control plane
vendors.pricing_tiers: Open Source (self-host gateway, free) / Developer (free) / Production ($49/month) / Enterprise (custom)

sso.value: OIDC and SAML 2.0 on the hosted/enterprise control plane; documented IdPs: Okta, Azure AD, generic OIDC/SAML; JIT-provisions first-time SSO users on verified domains. Not in the OSS gateway
sso.tier: Enterprise — pricing page lists 'SSO' only under the Enterprise plan; docs call it 'SSO support for enterprises'

scim.value: User provisioning/deprovisioning/updates + group→workspace provisioning with role mapping; documented IdPs: Azure AD, Okta (Okta SCIM requires a SAML app); verified domains only
scim.tier: not documented — docs live under 'Enterprise Offering' but no explicit plan banner, and SCIM is absent from the pricing page's tier lists

rbac.value: Org roles (Owner/Admin/Member) + workspace roles (Manager/Member) + per-API-key granular permissions across ~9 feature areas; workspace-scoped service-account and user API keys. Not in the OSS gateway
rbac.tier: Conflicting vendor statements: pricing page puts 'Role-Based Access Control, Service Account API Keys' on Production ($49/mo), while the access-control docs page carries the banner 'This is a Portkey Enterprise plan feature.'

audit_logs.value: Org-wide audit log of admin actions (timestamp, user, workspace, action, resource, status, client IP+country), 'Indefinite log retention'; export via Admin API GET /v1/audit-logs (JSON, filters, pagination); no bulk file export documented for audit logs specifically
audit_logs.tier: Enterprise — exact wording: 'This is a Portkey Enterprise plan feature.'

vendors.notes: The OSS repo is the data-plane gateway only; its README lists no SSO/SCIM/RBAC/audit for OSS ('The enterprise version offers advanced capabilities for org management, governance, security'). All identity/governance requires the hosted or enterprise control plane.

vendors.type: OSS gateway + Konnect SaaS / Kong Gateway Enterprise
vendors.pricing_tiers: Konnect: Free / Plus / Enterprise; self-managed: Kong Gateway (OSS) vs Kong Gateway Enterprise

sso.value: Konnect SSO via OIDC and SAML ('supports any OIDC or SAML-compliant provider'; Okta, Azure AD, Oracle IDCS, Keycloak verified). No admin/control-plane SSO documented for OSS Kong Gateway
sso.tier: Enterprise only — pricing FAQ verbatim: 'Advanced features like SSO and Audit Logs are only available with Enterprise'

scim.value: not documented for Konnect or Kong Gateway — SCIM pages exist only for the separate Insomnia product; Konnect instead maps IdP group claims to teams via OIDC/SAML (not SCIM)
scim.tier: n/a for the gateway (not documented); Insomnia SCIM is Insomnia-Enterprise

rbac.value: Konnect: teams + predefined/custom roles scoped org-wide, per resource type, per instance, per region. Self-managed Enterprise: RBAC entity with workspace-, endpoint- and entity-level permissions. Absent from OSS: zero rbac config keys in OSS kong.conf.default; how-to states 'This tutorial requires Kong Gateway Enterprise.'
rbac.tier: Konnect: from Plus tier (pricing lists 'API platform security - RBAC' under Plus); self-managed: Kong Gateway Enterprise only

audit_logs.value: Konnect: org audit logs webhooked to SIEM in ArcSight CEF / JSON / CrowdStrike CPS; retention 7 days then permanently deleted. Self-managed Enterprise: /audit/requests and /audit/objects Admin API endpoints, TTL via audit_log_record_ttl. No audit_log keys in OSS kong.conf.default
audit_logs.tier: Konnect: Enterprise only ('Advanced features like SSO and Audit Logs are only available with Enterprise'); self-managed: Enterprise Admin API

vendors.notes: Konnect's 7-day audit retention makes the SIEM webhook effectively mandatory for compliance. Kong's pricing page mixes Konnect and Insomnia tables — the SCIM line item belongs to Insomnia, not the gateway.

vendors.pricing_tiers: OSS free; API7 Enterprise (annual license by CPU cores); API7 Cloud (Standard / Premium)

sso.value: OSS: none for administration — Admin API uses a single shared admin key; openid-connect/saml-auth plugins authenticate proxied traffic, not the control plane. API7: Dashboard SSO via OIDC, SAML 2.0, LDAP (Keycloak, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, Google guides)
sso.tier: API7 Enterprise only (listed under 'Enterprise Features'); absent in OSS

scim.value: OSS: not documented. API7: 'SCIM provisions and de-provisions user accounts' via SCIM endpoint + token; IdP guides for Okta and Microsoft Entra ID; SCIM-labeled users must be deleted via the IdP. Introduced in API7 Enterprise 3.2.11

rbac.value: OSS: none for administration (all-or-nothing admin key; wolf-rbac is data-plane). API7: 'Super Admin is the only built-in role' + custom roles + IAM-style JSON permission policies with allow/deny and permission boundaries; scoping shown at gateway-group and published-service level

audit_logs.value: OSS: not documented. API7: records logins and all operations (time, operator, event type, resource, IP, source); 'retained for 180 days by default'; immutable with data masking; export in JSON or CSV

vendors.notes: Do not conflate APISIX data-plane auth plugins (openid-connect, saml-auth, wolf-rbac, authz-casbin — they protect proxied APIs) with control-plane identity, which OSS APISIX lacks entirely (single shared admin key).

vendors.pricing_tiers: OSS free (no paid tier of the OSS project itself; enterprise version sold as Alibaba Cloud APIG — separate row)

sso.value: not documented — console auth is a single local administrator account ('You need to initialize the administrator account on your first visit'); console repo lists login-management capabilities as a planned iteration
sso.tier: n/a — feature absent at any tier

rbac.value: not documented — single admin user model; no multi-user, org/team, or per-key console roles in docs or console repo

audit_logs.value: not documented for console/admin operations (no audit-log feature or export path found in docs or console repo)

vendors.notes: Data-plane auth plugins (basic-auth, key-auth, JWT, OIDC) authenticate proxied API traffic, not console operators. 'not documented' reflects vendor silence, not confirmed absence of code.

vendors.type: hosted — Alibaba Cloud Cloud-Native API Gateway / AI Gateway, the commercial version of Higress
vendors.pricing_tiers: Sold by instance capacity; identity/governance inherited from the Alibaba Cloud account plane (RAM / CloudSSO / ActionTrail), not gateway SKUs

sso.value: Alibaba Cloud RAM SAML 2.0 SSO at the cloud-account plane: role-based SSO (recommended) and user-based SSO; APIG security docs direct customers to RAM-role SSO
sso.tier: No cost or edition restriction documented — available to every Alibaba Cloud account (no SSO tax)

scim.value: CloudSSO SCIM 2.0 user/group provisioning from external IdPs; documented walkthroughs for Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak
scim.tier: Account-plane service (CloudSSO), not an APIG SKU feature; no paid-tier gating documented on the cited pages

rbac.value: RAM users, groups, roles with system + custom JSON policies (Effect/Action/Resource/Condition); RAM service code 'apig' with resource-level authorization down to individual gateway resources
rbac.tier: No tier gating documented — RAM is free account-plane infrastructure

audit_logs.value: ActionTrail records console + OpenAPI management events (incl. console sign-in); API Gateway has a documented audit-event list; delivery to Simple Log Service or OSS buckets; 90-day online query/download
audit_logs.tier: 90-day management-event retention free per account; delivery/extended storage billed at SLS/OSS rates; not gated by APIG SKU

vendors.notes: All four capabilities come from the Alibaba Cloud account plane (RAM / CloudSSO / ActionTrail) rather than gateway feature tiers. Caveat: CloudSSO pricing page not fetched; 'free' asserted only where a doc said so.

vendors.pricing_tiers: Free / Pay-as-you-go (5.5% platform fee) / Enterprise (custom agreement)

sso.value: SAML SSO via Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, or any custom SAML provider; self-serve setup (DNS domain verification + IdP connection) by org admins
sso.tier: Enterprise — docs: 'SSO is available for organizations on Enterprise plans'; pricing lists 'SSO/SAML' under Enterprise only

scim.value: 'SCIM Group Mappings': sync IdP groups to workspaces for automatic access provisioning; IdP-deactivated users lose org membership and their org-scoped API keys are deactivated (not auto-re-enabled on reactivation)
scim.tier: Enterprise (documented inside the Enterprise-gated SSO guide; not a separate pricing line item)

rbac.value: Two org-level roles only: Admin (full access) and Member; org admins control per-workspace access; members manage only their own keys, admins can view all org keys; no custom roles documented
rbac.tier: not documented (organization-management docs state no plan requirement; pricing lists 'Admin Controls' under Enterprise)

audit_logs.value: not documented — no admin-action audit log (member/role/key-change events) or SIEM path documented. What exists: usage/activity export as CSV or PDF (filter by period, group by model/key/creator) and Enterprise-page 'Unified Reporting'
audit_logs.tier: n/a — no audit log to gate; the activity export carries no stated tier, and 'Unified Reporting' is marketed on the Enterprise page

vendors.notes: Classic SSO-tax shape: SSO+SCIM Enterprise-gated; orgs/workspaces/2-role RBAC appear available below Enterprise. Biggest enterprise gap vs peers: no documented admin-action audit log.

vendors.type: hosted (identity inherited from the Vercel team plan)
vendors.pricing_tiers: Hobby (free) / Pro ($20/user/month) / Enterprise (custom); AI Gateway itself available on all three

sso.value: SAML SSO at the Vercel team level (AI Gateway inherits team identity); 20+ IdPs (Okta, Auth0, Entra, ADFS, OneLogin, Duo, JumpCloud, PingFederate, Keycloak, ...); SAML enforcement toggle
sso.tier: Enterprise included, or Pro via paid add-on at '$300 / month' ('Pro teams will first need to purchase the SAML SSO add-on'); not available on Hobby

scim.value: 'Directory Sync' (SCIM-style): auto invite/remove team members from the IdP directory (Okta, Google Directory, ...), IdP-group-to-role mapping
scim.tier: Enterprise only — 'Directory Sync is only available for Enterprise Teams'; NOT purchasable as a Pro add-on

rbac.value: Team roles (Owner, Member, Developer, Security, Billing, Viewer, Contributor) + project-level roles + composable permission groups; no per-AI-Gateway-API-key RBAC documented (gateway keys are team-scoped)
rbac.tier: Pro = team-level, Enterprise = team + project level (pricing page wording); Hobby has none

audit_logs.value: Team audit log (Owner role): CSV export (timestamp, action, actor, IP, user_agent, prev/next state; last-90-day exports) + SIEM streaming (S3, Splunk, Datadog, GCS, HTTP JSON/NDJSON; being replaced by 'Audit Log Drains'); covers team/project/member/env-var events, not AI-Gateway request-level events
audit_logs.tier: Enterprise only ('available to customers on enterprise plans')

vendors.notes: AI Gateway has no gateway-specific identity/governance — all four come from the underlying Vercel team plan. The SSO tax is explicit and priced ($300/mo on Pro); SCIM and audit logs cannot be bought on Pro at any price. Third-party claims of a $150/mo Pro SCIM add-on are contradicted by Vercel's own docs.

vendors.type: hosted (identity inherited from the Cloudflare account plane)
vendors.pricing_tiers: Account plans Free / Pro / Business / Enterprise; AI Gateway 'available on all plans' (its own gating uses Workers Free vs Workers Paid)

sso.value: Dashboard SSO connector enforces SSO to the Cloudflare dashboard (where AI Gateway is managed) with any IdP configured in Cloudflare One; SAML 2.0 explicitly documented (incl. Okta IdP-initiated)
sso.tier: All plans, free — exact wording: 'Cloudflare Dashboard SSO is available for free to all plans.' No SSO tax

scim.value: Dashboard SCIM user provisioning via Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or Authentik
scim.tier: Enterprise only — exact wording: 'Cloudflare dashboard SCIM provisioning is only available to Enterprise customers'

rbac.value: Account-scoped roles (70+ predefined), domain-scoped roles (~15), resource-scoped roles (Beta, limited resources); no AI-Gateway-specific role and no per-gateway/per-key RBAC documented
rbac.tier: Docs state no tier restriction; the launch blog shipped Domain Scoped Roles to Enterprise accounts — current docs do not restate a tier (flagged, not inferred)

audit_logs.value: 'Audit Logs are available on all plan types'; 18-month retention; export via dashboard CSV, REST API (GET /accounts/{id}/audit_logs), and Logpush to external storage
audit_logs.tier: All plans (view/CSV/API); Logpush export called out for Enterprise ('Enterprise customers can extend this using Logpush')

vendors.notes: All identity/governance inherited from the Cloudflare account plane, not AI-Gateway-specific. The one vendor in this matrix shipping dashboard SSO free on every plan. AI Gateway request-log Logpush (Workers Paid) is distinct from account audit logs.
